app.title: Censor Check
app.summary: A person loads a table of potency measurements, either a bundled example or their own CSV or database export. Columns are matched by name. They set a threshold for what counts as weak and the minimum group sizes, then run the check. The tool shows what an exact-values-only filter removes: per-category bars of the weak share before and after the filter, which can be limited to groups that could reach the threshold, and a table of how many records are kept and how many are lost. It then fits pooled and grouped censored-normal models to show how much dropping bounds overstates each group's mean. The person picks two categories to compare pooled against within-group, reads the checks for counter-screens and disguised ceilings, and exports a summary CSV, a results JSON or the figure as a PNG.

task.text: Measure what an exact-value filter removes from a table of censored measurements, estimate the bias that follows, and check whether pooled comparisons still hold inside the groups that produced the data.

data.text: A table of measurement records, each with a relation (exact, greater-than or less-than), a concentration value with units, the source paper it came from, the target or other category it belongs to, a compound identifier and a validity flag.
data.item: one reported potency record: a relation and a value for one compound against one target in one paper

stage.text: auditing censored records in a compiled potency table before modelling or comparing targets

mechanism.text: A settings form loads the table and runs every computation at once. The results are laid out as a long dashboard of headline metrics, per-category bar charts, accounting and estimate tables, a histogram of per-group shifts and verdict cards. A separate compare form picks two categories and redraws the pooled-versus-within-group difference chart. Changing an input marks the results as out of date and disables the exports until the check is run again.

field.text: censored-data (Tobit) audit of IC50 potency tables in medicinal chemistry

workflow.name: audit what a data filter removes and whether pooled comparisons hold within groups

steps.here: Pick the bundled subset or a file. Delimiters and column names are detected, and the matched columns are listed.

steps.step: set the rule and run the computation
steps.here: Set the weakness threshold in nM, the minimum records per paper and the minimum exact values for a shift, then press 'Run the check'.

The accounting table counts exact, right-censored, left-censored and validity-flagged records and how many the filter keeps. Bars show the weak share per target with all evidence and after the filter, with a toggle for 'only papers whose reported values reach the threshold'.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Pooled and grouped censored-normal fits give the mean overstatement, the between-paper and within-paper SDs, and a histogram of per-paper shifts with its median. A bar shows where the bounds sit relative to the threshold.

Choose stratum A, stratum B and which records to use. The chart shows the pooled difference, the pooled difference over shared papers only, and the Mantel–Haenszel within-paper difference, and flags a sign reversal.

steps.step: check for hidden problems in the records
steps.here: Verdict cards compare how often counter-screen and primary targets are censored, and compare ties at each paper's top exact value with ties in the interior.
Summary CSV per stratum, results JSON or the weak-share figure as PNG. These are disabled whenever the inputs have changed since the last run.

distinctive: Greater-than bounds are treated as measurements: they enter the likelihood as censored values, not as dropped rows.
Each paper is a group with its own mean and a shared within-group spread, so the tool separates between-paper from within-paper variation.
Pooled differences are set against within-paper differences weighted by Mantel–Haenszel, and a Simpson-style sign reversal is flagged.
A reachability restriction keeps only the groups whose highest reported value reaches the threshold, so weakness could have been recorded there at all.
A test for disguised ceilings looks for ties at each group's top exact value.
